dct_description_sm: The availability of nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) determines plant community structure and ecosystem carbon (C) storage in arctic tundra, and tundra soils typically have small pools of these limiting nutrients. Pulses of N and P during spring thaw as a result of thaw disturbance to soil and soil microbes may be critical for ecosystem functioning. Athough a substantial nutrient content has been characterized in arctic lakes during nival melt, a spring flush has seldom been reported in arctic tundra soil. The timing, the magnitude and the drivers of this flush, and the sensitivity to climate change, have not been previously described. Our goal is to characterize the soil biogeochemistry and soil microbial community at a high temporal frequency from the late winter to the late spring.
dct_title_s: Spring-thaw soil biogeochemistry and soil microbial succession in low arctic tundra, Daring Lake, NWT
